speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do they worsen after physical exertion? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CK, AChR antibodies.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC and CK results are pending, but have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech accompanying your double vision? Also, does swallowing food or liquids become difficult for you?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's helpful; since the AChR antibodies are pending, could you describe exactly which muscles in your upper limbs feel weak and whether you feel any fatigue in your eye muscles? REQUEST TEST: AChR antibodies; also, please return images of a fatigability test or electromyography (EMG) results if available.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography: Findings indicate decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor antibodies combined with EMG findings showing decreased muscle response on repetitive stimulation confirms this diagnosis, explaining your double vision, limb weakness, and difficulty with exertion.
